title: South Street Seaport Museum
summary: The Seaport Museum holds two photographs from Jeremy Dennis’s On This Site. Circassian Site recalls the ten Shinnecock people who drowned in 1876 helping the crew of the wrecked ship Circassian off Mecox Bay.
listing_image_alt: Circassian Site (2017) by Jeremy Dennis, from On This Site. The South Street Seaport Museum holds a print.
why_this_matters: The 1876 wreck of the Circassian is part of the history of New York shipping, and so are the ten Shinnecock people who drowned helping its crew. With this photograph in its collection, a maritime museum keeps their part in that story.
introduction_title: On This Site in the museum collection
introduction_content:
At the end of 2023 the South Street Seaport Museum acquired two photographs from Shinnecock artist Jeremy Dennis’s On This Site: Circassian Site (2017), which the museum catalogues as Circassian Shipwreck, and Winippague (2021).[1]

Circassian Site looks out from the shore at Mecox Bay in Bridgehampton, where the freight ship Circassian wrecked on December 30, 1876. Ten Shinnecock people drowned while helping its crew. Read the Circassian Shipwreck history.

Winippague shows Bergen Island in Jamaica Bay. The place name Winippague belongs to the island, which has been identified as a wampum-making place for Canarsie people. Read about Winippague.

In November 2025 Martina Caruso, the museum’s Director of Collections and Exhibitions, published a conversation with Dennis about documenting Shinnecock land in the museum’s Collections Chronicles.[1]
whereintheworld_content: The museum is at 12 Fulton Street in Lower Manhattan.[2] Collection photographs are not always on view, so ask the museum before you go if you hope to see them. Plan a visit or read the museum’s conversation with Jeremy Dennis.
